subject: storytime
title: The Little Red Hen
about: The folk tale of the hard-working hen whose friends will not help plant, cut or bake, and then all want to eat the bread. Most first graders already know it from kindergarten read-alouds, which makes it a good story to read on their own: a known plot and lines that repeat on every page. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, four pages long.
tip: Let him be the cat, the dog and the pig and say Not I in a different lazy voice each time.

book.author: a folk tale (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: Nobody wants to help, but everybody wants bread.

passage.text:
A little red hen lived on a farm.
She lived with a cat, a dog, and a pig.
One day she found some wheat seeds.
"Who will help me plant the wheat?" she asked.
"Not I," said the cat.
"Not I," said the dog.
"Not I," said the pig.
"Then I will do it myself," said the hen.
And she did.
***
The wheat grew tall.
"Who will help me cut the wheat?" she asked.
"Not I," said the cat.
"Not I," said the dog.
"Not I," said the pig.
"Then I will do it myself," said the hen.
And she did.
She took the wheat to the mill.
The mill made it into flour.
***
"Who will help me bake the bread?" she asked.
"Not I," said the cat.
"Not I," said the dog.
"Not I," said the pig.
"Then I will do it myself," said the hen.
And she did.
The bread smelled so good.
***
"Who will help me eat the bread?" she asked.
"I will!" said the cat.
"I will!" said the dog.
"I will!" said the pig.
"No," said the hen.
"You did not help me."
"So I will eat it myself."
And she did.
She ate it with her little chicks.
Yum!
If you want to share, you have to help.

cards.note: Everything in the story starts with the hen finding those seeds.

cards.q: What did the cat say when the hen asked for help?
cards.note: The cat, the dog and the pig all say the same two words, every time.

cards.q: Where did the little red hen live?
cards.note: A farm is where wheat can be planted and grown.

cards.q: What did the hen make with the flour?
cards.note: Seeds, then wheat, then flour, then bread: ask him to say the steps in order.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: First seeds, then tall wheat, then flour, then bread.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: She shared it with her chicks, not with the friends who would not help.

cards.q: How did the cat, dog and pig act when asked to help?
cards.note: Ask what the three friends could have done differently.
If you want to share the good part, you have to share the work.

cards.q: In the story, what is a 'mill'?
cards.note: A mill grinds wheat seeds into flour; long ago a big wheel did the grinding.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
